title: Eating-Out vs Cooking Cost Split
dataSources: Micro-spend transactions (`microspend:txn`), no-spend days (`nospend:day`), price-per-use items (`priceperuse:item`), cash-back rewards (`cashback:reward`).
app: Bank-transaction exports categorised for micro-spending, no-spend-day trackers, price-per-use logs, and cash-back / rewards feeds — sent to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=microspend:txn
| eval kind=case(category="restaurants","eating out",category="groceries","cooking",1=1,"other")
| where kind!="other"
| bin _time span=1mon
| stats sum(amount) as spend by kind _time
| sort - _time
description: Compares what you spend eating out versus buying groceries each month, revealing the true cost of convenience.
value: The eating-out-versus-cooking split is one of the biggest controllable levers in a food budget.
implementation: Categorise food spending in `index=personal`; schedule monthly and compare eating out to groceries.
visualization: Stacked column chart of eating-out versus grocery spend.
grandmaExplanation: It compares what you spend eating out versus cooking at home, showing the real cost of takeaways.
